title: The dispatch picks the model from the score, and the record says which one ran
name: The dispatch picks the model from the
description:
`dispatch.ts` reads `config.dispatch.host` in four places — `checkHost` at :103, `adapterFor` at :110, `startRun` at :122 and `startAgent` at :147. Put one resolution in front of all four: read the node's brief, turn `complexity` into a tier through `dispatch.thresholds`, and look the model up in the table for the adapter `dispatch.host` resolves to. `adapterFor` still finds the adapter by program name, so whatever the resolution produces must not break that — an unknown host is refused rather than defaulted, and it should stay refused.

Record the model on the run beside the host: `startRun` already stores which host ran, and “why did this node cost that” is unanswerable without it. Render it where the host is already shown, in `sober logs` and the dashboard's run panel.

Settings that govern how a run is prepared and judged are read from the base ref and never from the branch being worked on (ADR 0019). The model is one of them and must come through `settings(paths, options.base)` like the rest of `dispatch` — read from its own branch, a dispatched agent could raise its own model on its own dispatch.

brief.approach: Complexity 7 / 10: this threads one dispatch-time choice through persisted run data and three user-facing surfaces, with compatibility-sensitive schema work and integration coverage. In `packages/core/src/dispatch.ts`, after reading base-ref settings and before `checkHost`, load the node brief, call the existing `tierFor(config.dispatch.thresholds, brief.complexity)`, and resolve the command line with `hostForTier`; an unscored brief uses `dispatch.host` with no tier, while a configured tier uses its line and an empty tier uses the recorded fallback. Use that single resolved line consistently for `checkHost`, `adapterFor`, attended-mode errors, `startAgent`, and `startRun`, so unknown commands remain refused before worktree creation and the refusal names the selected tier. Extend `packages/schema/src/run.ts` and `packages/core/src/run.ts` with backward-compatible/defaulted facts sufficient to render the selected tier and whether `dispatch.host` was the fallback while retaining `host` as the exact command line that ran; local run records are not board migrations. Update run-event construction only as required by the schema. In `packages/cli/src/work.ts` and the existing dashboard log/run-panel components under `apps/dashboard/src/logs/`, render the same host line, tier, and fallback wording from the run record rather than re-reading current config. Add focused core/schema tests and integration cases in `test/integration/dispatch.test.ts` for high/mid/low thresholds, configured tier selection, missing-tier fallback, null-complexity default behavior, unknown selected hosts, and base-ref config authority. Keep adapters and model-flag parsing unchanged: each tier value is already a complete host command line under ADR 0058.

acceptance.run: pnpm vitest run packages/core/src/config.test.ts packages/schema/src/run.test.ts packages/core/src/run.test.ts test/integration/dispatch.test.ts
acceptance.proves: Threshold mapping, run-record compatibility, selected tier commands, fallback behavior, refusal paths, and base-ref authority are covered end to end.
Every run producer and CLI/dashboard consumer agrees on the extended persisted run shape.

acceptance.run: git grep -q 'tierFor' -- packages/core/src/dispatch.ts && git grep -q 'hostForTier' -- packages/core/src/dispatch.ts && git grep -q 'fallback' -- packages/schema/src/run.ts packages/core/src/run.ts packages/cli/src/work.ts apps/dashboard/src/logs
acceptance.proves: Dispatch uses the shared config resolution and the fallback fact reaches both terminal and dashboard surfaces.
The public export ceilings remain unchanged.
Biome and secretlint remain clean across the touched implementation and tests.
